subject: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist & next steps

Hi John / Sarah,

Thanks again for the time today — appreciate you walking us through Acme's customer support flows and the sample transcripts. Per our discussion, attached is a concise shortlist of models we recommend for your pilot along with rationale and links to the benchmark report and prompt set we'll use for your evals. High-level summary below: 

- Recommended shortlist (tradeoffs summarized):
  * rw-3b-q4 (Redwood-rw-3B, 4-bit quant): Lowest latency / lowest cost, good for short-turn conversational assistants where response time is critical.
  * rw-13b-8bit (Redwood-rw-13B, 8-bit): Balanced latency + quality — solid for general-purpose summarization and triage.
  * llama2-13b-chat-16k (Meta Llama 2 13B, 16K context): Best quality on longer-context summarization and nuanced instruction-following; higher cost and slightly higher latency.

- Key tradeoffs we measured (from your sample workload):
  * Cost estimate (hosted) per 1M tokens: rw-3b-q4 ~ $12, rw-13b-8bit ~ $28, llama2-13b-chat-16k ~ $52 (est; depends on batching/kv-cache).
  * Median p95 latency (single-request, us-west): rw-3b-q4 ~ 80ms, rw-13b-8bit ~ 220ms, llama2-13b-chat-16k ~ 480ms.
  * Quality notes: rw-13b-8bit shows substantially fewer hallucinations on your templates vs rw-3b-q4; llama2-13b-chat provides best long-form coherence on >8k context.

Attachments included: acme_model_shortlist_v1.pdf (one-pager with numbers) and acme_prompt_set_v1.zip (prompt templates and eval prompts). Benchmark report link and HubSpot deal link below.

Next steps I suggest:
1) You confirm the shortlist and the primary success metric you want us to optimize for (latency/cost vs accuracy).
2) We kick off a 2-week pilot using a gated eval harness (we'll run the prompt set you provided + our expanded prompt variations).
3) Rishi will follow up on Dedicated capacity pricing if you want a reserved pool/throughput guarantee for the pilot.

If that sounds good, we'll schedule the kickoff for early next week.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

Hi John — good questions, answered inline below and attached the benchmark/metrics doc for transparency.

1) Success metrics & rubric:
- We'll run the prompt set (attached) with labeled ground-truth where available (your sample transcripts + our augmented cases). Evaluation metrics: accuracy/precision on intent slots, F1 on entity extraction, false-hallucination rate (percentage of responses that contain facts not supported by the transcript), and end-to-end routing latency. We'll provide the full rubric in the attached PDF (https://redwood-inference.s3.amazonaws.com/acme/benchmarks/acme-benchmark-report-20260311.pdf).

2) Benchmark prompts & eval harness:
- Attached prompt set (acme_prompt_set_v1.zip) contains: base prompts, few-shot exemplars, adversarial prompts, and long-context cases. We'll run each prompt across the three shortlisted models with identical sampling settings and measure token-level differences and qualitative failure modes.

3) Failure modes & prompt tweaks:
- rw-3b-q4: occasional back-fill hallucinations on very sparse context; mitigate with stricter system prompt and explicit "only use information present in the transcript" guardrails.
- rw-13b-8bit: best balance; occasional entity conflation in long threads — recommend a short retrieval check (simple doc-match) before generation for named-entity heavy flows.
- llama2-13b-chat-16k: strongest long-context coherence but tends to be more verbose and can hallucinate confident-sounding but incorrect resolutions; use a conservative temperature (0.0–0.2) and post-generation fact-check shim.

4) Budget: For a 2-week pilot running your sample volume (approx 200k tokens/day), estimates:
- rw-13b-8bit: ~$5.5k — within the $7k pilot cap (assuming standard batching and no heavy long-context runs).
- rw-3b-q4: ~$2k.
- llama2-13b-chat-16k: ~$9–10k (likely above the pilot cap unless we limit context length or run fewer cases).

Given your accuracy-first requirement, rw-13b-8bit looks like the right starting point and fits the budget. If you'd like, we can start the pilot with a mixed strategy: run the rw-13b-8bit as primary and sample-run llama2-13b-chat on a subset of long-context cases to validate differences.

Attached: acme-benchmark-report-20260311.pdf (detailed results), acme_model_shortlist_v1.pdf (one-pager).

If that approach works, confirm and we'll schedule the pilot kickoff + Rishi will share a pilot quote.

Best,
Marissa
